title: Loop over an array state
summary: Proves the compiler's loop whose state is an Array Float: a copy of the initial array, then one call per index that returns the next state, with the previous state released, inside the Live invariant of a composite function.
premises: An Implements theorem for the callee, which returns an Array Float
The five loop locals are distinct, below scratch, and apart from the source local, and scratch is below the number of locals
Live before the loop, with the initial array borrowed at the source local's pointer
The count evaluates to n in every state that frames the state before the loop
The callee's need at each index and prefix state is at most bound, and the bytes used plus the copy plus n times bound fit in the room
At each index, the arguments evaluate to values that represent F l x, given the Live invariant with the state at its head
result: Live with the bytes used plus the copy plus n times bound, and LeanExe.loop n init (fun l x => g (F l x)) at the head of the live temporaries, whose pointer the state local holds, in a state that frames the one before the loop.
